title: The Quantum Nose Test
hook: Swap hydrogen for deuterium. Hear the molecule fall.
sub: A contested theory says your nose reads molecular vibrations. We slowed three odorants' vibrations 120 billion times into hearing range and ran them through a 20-qubit quantum blur. You get to smell by ear.
you_control: Pick a molecule (acetophenone, cyclopentadecanone, muscone): it rides a sniff up the nose on an anatomy plate, and a loupe shows it on the mucus at molecular scale
Sniff: hear a sniff, watch the puffs ride the airflow, and the odorant land and bind (the neuron fires, the bulb flashes)
Play its vibrational chord: the magnified atoms wobble with the notes, and the caption names the loudest line
Swap H for D while it sounds: the hydrogen lines glide down 5.35 semitones and a neutron flies into every hydrogen
Blur the chord through blur-midi-v1: strength 0.25/0.5/1 x reach local/halfway/global (9 real jobs)
Play the WAV deliverable for the current molecule, isotope and blur setting, and stop it, from the instrument
Drag the hypothetical receptor gap in Fig. d: when it matches a line the electron tunnels and kicks that mode
Take the blind test: pick the deuterated sample, optionally with pitch disguised, scored against chance; the pixel nose sniffs along
Open evidence-for and evidence-against drawers that load molecules and shade bands on the instrument
qubits_note: Computed, not reported by the engine: each of the 6 tracks is a piano roll of 77-111 pitch rows (7 qubits) x 6,720 time steps (13 qubits) = 20 qubits per pass, the engine maximum (qubits param 20). Quantum Blur grid rule ceil(log2 w)+ceil(log2 h).
deliverables: wav/<setting>/<molecule>_<H|D>.wav (60 files: input score + 9 blur settings x 6 chords)
web/audio/chords/<setting>/<molecule>_<H|D>.mp3 (60 files: every chord WAV, played on the page)
honesty: The vibration theory of olfaction is stated as unproven and contested; vibrational lines are approximate textbook values with harmonic H->D estimates; the quantum blur ran on Atlas's classical statevector simulator and is a sound effect, not a model of tunnelling or a nose; qubit count is computed from the grid rule.
